A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OSA despite the changed title and formatting. All 20 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original noisy-label retrieval and classification experiments, estimator analyses, noise-detection results and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical investigations and adds CC3M results and a scoring-function comparison in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the pretrained estimator, random-pair estimate of the similarity shift, cubic scoring function, optional GMM-based domain adaptation and loss reweighting. The additional scoring functions are comparison variants; the prescribed OSA procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: The same tasks and domains remain, including image-text matching, WebFG classification, CARS98N retrieval and SDM style tests. v2 explicitly describes CC120K as a subset of CC3M, so its added full-CC3M experiment documents a scale extension within the existing web image-text coverage rather than a distinct task or population.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix D.2 and Table 8 add Linear and Cosine weighting comparators against the selected High-Degree scorer. The comparator sets in the retained benchmark experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation at full CC3M scale and a three-scorer comparison on MS-COCO with 50% noise. The architecture comparison now reports only the 1K evaluation pool instead of both 1K and 5K. Existing metrics and Appendix A training settings remain unchanged; CC3M-specific splits and budgets are unspecified.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.2 tests sensitivity to the scoring function, with Table 8 showing the High-Degree function best or tied across metrics. Existing estimator, domain-adaptation, noise-ranking and SDM analyses remain, while the architecture analysis loses its 5K results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for benchmark performance. The existing distribution means and variances are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises the 50%-noise CLIP+OSA results: MS-COCO 5K i2t/t2i R@1 changes from 64.0/47.9 to 64.7/48.6, also reflected in the estimator table. v2 adds CC3M and scorer-comparison results and removes the 5K architecture entries. The old OSA row reappears as Linear in v2 Table 8, leaving the revision's provenance unclear; most retained results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds explicit piecewise mathematical definitions of the linear and cosine scoring alternatives in Equations 32–33. The central boundary-shift and Gaussian-output theorems, their assumptions and their proof arguments remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain orthogonality-based noise separation and model-agnostic, transferable noise mitigation with one additional inference and low overhead. The new title and consolidated contribution list primarily reframe claims already present in v1.

C2.justification: v1 calls domain adaptation unnecessary; v2 qualifies this to not always necessary in Section 4.5. v2 also adds explanations linking scorer performance to gradient behavior, Gaussian features to mean-field arguments, and CC3M practicality to NPC's memory requirements. The limitation concerning actual large-scale pretraining remains.

D1.justification: v2 removes the approximately 24 GB memory-use figure from the timing analysis and adds an explanation of NPC's memory-bank failure on CC3M. The code URL and core Appendix A implementation settings remain unchanged. A specific reproduction protocol for CC3M is not supplied.

R1.justification: The introduction adds positioning against pretrained-model noise methods, including CLIPCleaner, Wei et al. and Liang et al., alongside scaling and dataset references. Appendix C.3 adds mean-field references. Appendix B.1 also changes its description of NPC from one forward and one backward pass to two backward passes, resolving a discrepancy with the retained main-text description.

P1.justification: The title, introduction, boundary-analysis narrative and several result summaries are substantially revised. Multiple experimental discussions move into a new Appendix D, the contribution list is consolidated, and separate Limitations and Ethic Statement sections are introduced.

P2.justification: The paper changes throughout from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 2 is redrawn to illustrate debiasing, and Figure 1's similarity axes are relabeled. Numerous tables move or change structure, including the shortened architecture table, expanded CC120K/CC3M table and new scoring-function table.

improvement.justification: The scoring-function ablation and full-CC3M evaluation provide useful additional support for design and scalability, while the domain-adaptation conclusion becomes better qualified. These gains are limited by underspecified CC3M procedures, NPC's unavailable CC3M accuracy results, unexplained revisions to the 50%-noise scores and removal of the 5K architecture evidence.
